name: Ansel Perry
life: “I still remember a shop window covered with cardboard for a whole season.” People around the approach to Seabright Court know Ansel by a small Monday habit. Ansel likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: My shop window went through in one of our old rows. I want regular payments for the glass and no speeches.
appearance: Ansel has a small notch in the left eyebrow. Look for a high puff tied with plain cord. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is an olive canvas jacket with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. In conversation Ansel holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Ansel finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
agenda: To get a regular repayment for the window.
family: Frank Moran is Ansel’s younger cousin. Ansel asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Frank remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *Station steps in rain*, Frank says, “I was handing out biscuits and learned that offering a uniformed stranger food takes nerve on both sides.”
connections: Katherine Nielsen. An old window bill and a found wage slip bring the young worker's finances into two households.

reactions.situation: An old customer arrives during the new warehouse shift
reactions.response: Ansel asks the two people to talk away from the work floor and leaves disclosure to the new hire.

reactions.situation: An unfamiliar person asks for directions but cannot read the street signs
reactions.response: Ansel draws the route by its turns and entrances and has the person show which turn comes first.

reactions.situation: When somebody waves from across traffic
reactions.response: Ansel waits at the corner to hear their voice and give them a proper answer.
